research_rationale: Executive Order 5930 (Herbert Hoover, October 6, 1932; register and WPA agree on the date and on Schedule A, Subdivision VII, Post Office Department, paragraph 6) is held in the Hoover Public Papers volume II OFR compilation (government printed copy, graded official compilation). Its text has two parts: an operative lead amending Schedule A and a single paragraph 6. Paragraph 6 limits itself to the present holiday or seasonal business "from this date to February 1, 1933 .", so the order ended by its own terms on that date. The date is recorded inclusive (the order runs through February 1, 1933); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when February 1 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No later order, statute or rule extended it: the packet's number lookup over 33,118 held texts finds no other text citing Executive Order 5930, and the three machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog 1937 onward) record no hit; the catalog search cannot see anything before 1937, so the pre-1937 period rests on the held-text number lookup alone.
savings_reason: The order contains no saving, transfer or residual clause: its only command adds paragraph 6 to Schedule A, Subdivision VII, for temporary Postal Service workers during the holiday or seasonal business "from this date to February 1, 1933 ."; the packet's number lookup over the held texts found no later order citing Executive Order 5930, and the current-law searches found no hit, so no independent or surviving command was located.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end was found: the packet's number lookup over the held texts finds no other text naming Executive Order 5930, and the order's own date limit falls on February 1, 1933, less than four months after signing; nothing held revokes or supersedes it earlier.
scope_check: The inventory has two items, the lead amending Schedule A, Subdivision VII, and paragraph 6; both were checked against the whole held text, which ends with the signature, the date October 6, 1932 and the number line, so nothing else is commanded.
independent_command_check: The lead and paragraph 6 form one command (the amendment consists only of the added paragraph), so the lead has no independent life beyond paragraph 6; no other command exists in the order.
savings_check: No saving clause exists in the held text, and no later instrument is held that preserves actions taken under it; the search lookups produced no hits.
